entries.title: Payroll corrections after the cut-off change
entries.detail: Moved the timesheet cut-off at a 48-person joinery from Friday noon to Thursday 4pm in February 2025. Correction runs fell from 9 in the prior six months to 2 in the next six.

figure.measures: off-cycle payroll correction runs per six months at one client
figure.basis: own run log, same headcount both periods

entries.words: The software was fine. The deadline was in the wrong place.

entries.title: The one-page overtime sheet
entries.detail: Wrote a single-page overtime rules sheet for a metal fabricator in 2024 that replaced a 14-page policy. Supervisors pin it by the clock.
entries.words: If it does not fit on the wall it does not get read.

entries.title: Stopped recommending weekly pay runs
entries.detail: Recommended weekly pay to every shop-floor client until 2023. Three clients moved to fortnightly and reported fewer advance requests, not more.
entries.before: Weekly pay is kinder to hourly staff.
entries.after: Predictable pay is kinder than frequent pay.

entries.title: The holiday accrual I got wrong
entries.detail: Misread a carry-over clause for a 30-person bakery in 2022. Reissued 30 statements and refunded my fee for the quarter.
entries.price: One quarter's fee and an uncomfortable all-hands at 5am.

entries.title: The supervisor with the shoebox
entries.detail: A night supervisor kept every amended timesheet for 6 years in a shoebox because he did not trust the system. In 2021 the shoebox settled a dispute the system could not.

entries.title: Payroll belongs in operations, not finance
entries.detail: Have argued since 2020 that payroll questions should be answered on the shop floor the same day. Lost one retainer over it.
entries.against: Finance directors who want one reporting line.
entries.price: One retainer, and a reputation for being stubborn about org charts.

entries.title: Eleven years in-house before going independent
entries.detail: Ran payroll in-house for a 400-person furniture maker from 2009 to 2020 before starting the studio.

entries.title: Quarterly payroll health check
entries.detail: A fixed-scope review for manufacturers under 100 staff, first run in 2023, 17 completed so far.

sample_lines: The software was fine. The deadline was in the wrong place.
